title: Outage: the API server will not start after last night's manifest edit

lines.text: 08:30 alert: kubectl and the CI pipeline get 'connection refused' from https://10.0.0.10:6443; the web Deployment must scale out for the 09:15 traffic peak
Change log, last night: 'tuned kube-apiserver flags in the static pod manifest' (no review)
kubeadm reset: /etc/kubernetes/manifests and the etcd data directory removed; the control plane is gone
kubelet: a second static pod from kube-apiserver-backup.yaml tries to bind port 6443
09:15 traffic peak: the HPA cannot scale web without the API; web is saturated and timing out

objective: Troubleshoot cluster components: static pod manifests for the API server, controller manager, scheduler and etcd, their flags and certificates, and reading their logs when kubectl itself fails

Read in primary text from the kubernetes/website main branch (raw Markdown source of kubernetes.io) through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-14. Relevant text: the kubelet 'periodically scans the directory and creates/deletes static Pods as YAML/JSON files appear/disappear there'; deleting the mirror Pod with kubectl does not stop it ('the kubelet doesn't remove the static Pod'); if a container is stopped manually the kubelet 'will notice and will restart the Pod'.

Read in primary text from the kubernetes/website main branch (raw Markdown) through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-14. Relevant text: with the API server down you are 'unable to stop, update, or start new pods, services, replication controller'; 'existing pods and services should continue to work normally unless they depend on the Kubernetes API'; 'On systemd-based systems, you may need to use journalctl instead of examining log files.' crictl appears under 'What's next' for debugging nodes. The crictl and kubelet output lines in the scenario are authored renderings.

Read 2026-11-16 on kubernetes.io (page modified 2024-09-18; summarizing fetch with quotes). Control plane rows: TCP inbound 6443 'Kubernetes API server', used by all; TCP inbound 2379-2380 'etcd server client API', used by kube-apiserver and etcd; 10250 Kubelet API; 10259 kube-scheduler; 10257 kube-controller-manager. The page notes etcd can also run externally or on custom ports. The scenario's etcd client port 2379 and API server port 6443 match.

brief.situation: You are the Kubernetes administrator for Brightwater Media, a fictional publisher. At 08:30 kubectl and the CI pipeline get 'connection refused' from the API server of cluster prod-1 (one kubeadm control plane node, cp1, and two workers). The web Deployment's pods are still serving, but the 09:15 traffic peak needs the autoscaler to add pods.
handover: Last night someone tuned kube-apiserver flags in its static pod manifest.
You have root on cp1, with crictl and journalctl.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the control plane, the kubelet and the web Deployment.
Each command takes a minute; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close the outage, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: how you diagnosed a control plane that kubectl could not reach, what you changed and how, and how you knew it was fixed.

parts.label: Without kubectl
parts.criteria: Goes to the node: crictl for the exited container and its logs, the kubelet journal, and the manifest flags; reads the etcd port mismatch.
parts.modelAnswer: kubectl was refused, so I worked on cp1: crictl ps showed kube-apiserver exiting while etcd ran; its logs showed it dialing 127.0.0.1:2397; the manifests showed etcd on 2379 and --etcd-servers on 2397.

parts.label: The change
parts.criteria: Backs up the manifest outside /etc/kubernetes/manifests, edits the flag in place and lets the kubelet recreate the static pod; explains why kubectl delete, a kubelet restart or kubeadm reset do not help.
parts.modelAnswer: I copied the manifest to /root (a copy in the manifests directory would become a second static pod), then fixed --etcd-servers to 2379. The kubelet watches that directory and recreated the pod. kubectl cannot delete anything without the API server, restarting the kubelet reloads the same flag, and kubeadm reset deletes etcd's data.

parts.label: Verified
parts.criteria: kubectl get nodes works and the API is up before the 09:15 peak; proposes review of manifest changes.
parts.modelAnswer: kubectl get nodes returned all three nodes Ready at about 08:40, before the peak. Manifest changes now go through review and a backup outside the directory.

scoring.modelReasoning: kubectl is refused, so work on the control plane node. crictl ps shows kube-apiserver exiting and restarting while etcd runs; crictl logs shows it dialing 127.0.0.1:2397; the manifests show etcd listening on 2379 and --etcd-servers set to 2397 by last night's edit. Back the manifest up outside /etc/kubernetes/manifests (the kubelet runs every manifest in that directory), fix the flag in place, and the kubelet recreates the static pod. kubectl delete needs the API server, restarting the kubelet reloads the same flag, and kubeadm reset deletes etcd's data. Existing pods keep serving, but nothing can scale until the API is back, so finish before the 09:15 peak and confirm with kubectl get nodes.
